title: What is a Quiet Aircraft Cabin?
excerpt: Cabin sound levels vary greatly between aircraft types. Understanding dB SIL and what the numbers actually mean for passenger comfort — and why consistency across the cabin matters as much as the headline figure.

title: Noise, Stress and Fatigue
excerpt: The relationship between in-flight noise exposure and post-flight fatigue is well-documented. Here's why cabin sound levels matter beyond mere comfort — and what a properly insulated aircraft does for crew and passenger endurance.

title: Active vs. Passive Noise Cancellation
excerpt: Active noise cancellation addresses only low-frequency bands in a limited area. A properly engineered passive system delivers consistent levels throughout the aircraft, requires no power, and no pre-flight programming.

title: How Much Confidence Do We Have in Achieving Targeted Noise Levels?
excerpt: Aircraft owners often ask how well a cabin insulation project will perform before the work begins. Here's what acoustic experience, imaging technology, and a comprehensive noise reduction plan can — and cannot — predict.

title: Using a Noise Reduction Plan to Limit Uncertainty
excerpt: A holistic approach — treating interior, ECS, and insulation simultaneously — consistently outperforms piecemeal treatments. We explain why, and what the data says about untreated noise sources masking each other.

title: Aircraft Insulation Basics
excerpt: There is more inside a business aircraft wall panel than most operators realize. This primer covers the materials, layering logic, dBA vs. dB SIL metrics, and certification considerations behind a modern acoustic insulation system.

title: Designing ADMI Mission Interiors for Demanding Environments
excerpt: An All Day Mission Interior is not simply a reconfigured cabin — it is a human-factors engineering problem that must balance crew endurance, equipment density, acoustic environment, and airworthiness across 12-hour missions.

title: Luminary Air Group Adds VIP Interior Capabilities
excerpt: Luminary welcomes a new cabinet shop in Richmond Hill, GA — expanding capability to full VIP cabinetry fabrication, green aircraft completions, and installations across all Boeing, Airbus, and Gulfstream platforms.

title: Luminary Receives Supplier Approval from Gulfstream
excerpt: Gulfstream Aerospace Corporation has granted Luminary Air Group supplier approval for materials, parts, and services for thermal and acoustic insulation treatments — a testament to Luminary's quality processes.

title: FAA Issues Quality Manual Approval and PMA to Luminary Air Group
excerpt: The FAA has completed its review of Luminary Air Group's quality system and confirmed the company meets 14 CFR airworthiness requirements. Parts Manufacturer Approval (PMA) has been granted.

title: Luminary Receives Multi-Aircraft Award for VVIP Insulation from Boeing
excerpt: Luminary Air Group was awarded a multi-aircraft contract by Boeing to design, build, and install thermal/acoustic insulation systems on VVIP aircraft operated by one of Boeing's customers.

title: Luminary Appointed Distributor of Teledyne ACES® Cabin Air Monitor
excerpt: Luminary Air Group has been appointed by Teledyne Controls as a distributor of ACES® — a real-time cabin air quality monitoring system designed for the business aviation market.
